paper_id: Rethinking Regularization Methods for Knowledge Graph Completion
title: Rethinking Regularization Methods for Knowledge Graph Completion
motivation: KGC models suffer from overfitting by learning noise in training data, limiting generalization and performance upper bounds
problem_framing: Reconceptualize regularization not just as overfitting mitigation but as a lever to break original performance ceilings; existing regularizers don't generalize to non-TDB models
key_insight: Selectively penalizing only large-magnitude embedding components while discarding noise-like small components improves generalization more than uniform penalization
method_signature: SPR: rank-based sparse regularization that masks small embedding components via cumulative-sum thresholding δ
evaluation_criteria: MRR, Hits@1/3/10 on WN18RR, FB15K-237, YAGO3-10; also UMLS, Kinship, TKGC datasets
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Regularization is a 'double-edged sword': both too-high and too-low rates degrade below no-regularization baseline; δ must be tuned per model
thinking_moves: 从观察到的训练/验证差距反推过拟合问题的普遍性
把正则化从'防止过拟合'重新frame成'突破性能上界'
通过对比Dropout与SPR的方差结构, 从理论上区分有效/无效mask
用信息论直觉(信号噪声比)设计稀疏化准则
